content.thinking:
I need to plan the whole scene carefully before writing it out in one pass, without testing along the way. I'm picturing a koala at realistic size, roughly 0.75m sitting upright, clinging naturally to a vertical eucalyptus branch mounted on a stand, in a relaxed, readable resting pose.

I'm weighing a few setups: a koala hugging a vertical trunk with limbs wrapped around it, versus sitting in the fork of a branch with its back against the trunk and arms gripping a forward branch. I think the simplest and most natural option is the hugging pose — body vertical against the trunk, arms and legs wrapped around it, trunk rising from a base disc stand.

I'll go with a fork design instead: a branch running along Z from the trunk, with the koala's bum nestled near the base and legs straddling either side, hind feet gripping the branch.

For the arms, I'll have them reach forward-down to grip the branch ahead, with the torso leaning slightly forward over it. I'm positioning the hips, shoulders, and head heights relative to the branch so the proportions read as a realistically seated koala.

Rather than one giant trunk, I'll build a taller slender trunk topped with eucalyptus leaf clusters, keeping overall model height around 1.4 units. I'm sketching the skeleton now — hips as root joint, then a spine chain curving up through chest, neck, to head using a smooth path of coordinates.

I'll just reference spine.joints[2] directly as the parent for head, letting the hips root and spine1 overlap in position which seems fine. Now I'm shaping the koala's head as a wide ellipsoid with big round ears and a huge black nose, scaling a sphere geometry to get that squashed head shape.

For coloring, I'm using cellPaint with dithering to apply a grey fur ramp shaded by surface normal and noise, since it evaluates at world position rather than needing UVs. I want the belly and chest to come out lighter/cream where the normal faces downward, plus white ear fringes and a black nose to match the koala look.

I'll limit the cream paint to the torso only, keeping arms and legs grey, then work out the ears as flattened disc shapes positioned on the sides of the head, angled outward and forward, with smaller cream inner-ear discs and tufts layered on top.

For the tufts, I'm figuring out whether to use fur cards or a ring of small cream shapes around the ear rim, trying to work out the right local coordinate frame so the ring orients correctly around each ear's normal direction.

Automatic bone inference seems ambiguous near the ear, since the nearest joint/bone segment isn't clearly head or jaw. Safer to just explicitly pass `bone: head` in every part/spike option rather than rely on nearest-joint logic.

I'll use absolute world coordinates everywhere with explicit bone assignments to avoid orientation confusion, and now I'm working out the jaw structure — a small lower jaw box joined at the head, plus an upper muzzle sphere and a separate nose piece positioned near the mouth.

For the nose I'll go with a pixel-art styled box using a tiny textured tile rather than a plain sphere, since koalas have a big flat black nose that reads better pixelated. Now I'm figuring out eye placement — small black beady eyes positioned symmetrically on the head sphere's front surface, accounting for the sphere's radius and center so they sit correctly on the curved face.

Working through the muzzle, nose, and mouth geometry — placing a lighter muzzle sphere, a protruding nose box in front of it, and a thin dark mouth line below, adjusting z-depths so each piece sits naturally on the surface without clipping oddly.

I also want to add cheek fluff and fur texture: cream-colored spheres for cheek tufts, plus scattered fur cards across the torso using a tinted pixel texture to give a soft, fuzzy coating over the body.

For the torso itself, I'm sweeping a rounded pear shape along the spine chain, giving the koala a rotund belly with varying radii that bulge larger in the lower-middle section and taper toward the shoulders.

Setting seat branch y to 0.37, then laying out the spine path with four control points rising from the hips to the upper torso, with radii tapering from wider at the base to narrower near the top for a natural rounded profile.

Now I'm sweeping the body geometry along the spine chain to generate the torso mesh with rounded caps, keeping the hip joint as the root parent so the chain sweep starts cleanly at the base. I'm positioning the head as a slightly flattened ellipsoid above the torso, checking that its bottom edge overlaps enough with the torso's top to avoid any visible gap at the neck.

Since koalas have essentially no visible neck, I'm placing the head joint close to the spine's top joint, with the jaw as a child joint aimed outward for mouth articulation. For the arms, I'm working out shoulder and hand placement so the koala's forelimbs reach forward and grip a branch positioned along the Z-axis, calculating the limb segment lengths needed so the two-bone arm chain spans the distance from shoulder to the gripping hand.

I'm defining the arm joint chains with shoulder, elbow, and wrist names, setting up bend direction hints so the elbow angles outward and back naturally, and planning to sweep the limbs with tapering radii while giving the hands two opposable digits for gripping.

For the hands, I'm simplifying to simple single-joint digits per finger rather than full capsule chains, creating a handful of digit joints per wrist angled to curl over a branch for grip.

Working out finger coordinates to wrap over the branch top...

That checks out as a reasonable bend length. I'm checking shoulder placement against torso radius to avoid overlap, nudging shoulder x inward slightly, and setting arm radius thinner near the shoulder. For the hind legs, I'm positioning the hips so the thighs come forward with knees splayed out, and placing the hind feet gripping the underside of the branch lower down.

Working out the knee bend direction and foot placement so toes wrap around the branch's side surface, keeping the foot just outside the branch radius.

The torso bottom resting on the branch works fine for the bum. For the hind leg chain I'll set up hip, knee, and ankle joints with the limb returning three points for two spans plus a tip, parented off the hip socket at x=±0.11. Arm chains should parent to the last spine joint near the shoulders, aligning with where the chest aims toward the next point.

For colors I'm going with grey fur overall, darker grey-black for feet and hand paw pads, dark grey digits, and off-white claw spikes at the digit tips. I'll skip a real tail joint but add a small fluffy rump bump instead. For the branch stand, I'm sizing a wood-stained cylinder disc as the base with a smaller stepped plate on top.

Now I'm refining the plinth into a stacked square wooden base with pixel plank texture, then sweeping a leaning trunk from the back using curved points rising from near the base up past head height. I'm deciding to parent all the static stand and trunk geometry to the hips bone since there's only one root joint, even though that means the stand moves with the hips rotation.

I'm now working out the seat/branch geometry extending from the trunk toward the koala's hips and hands, tuning the catmull path points, radii, and cap extension so the branch aligns properly under the torso bottom at y≈0.38.

I'm also adding two more upward branches off the trunk for secondary foliage placement, and planning eucalyptus leaf sprays—elongated blade-shaped leaves textured like pixel cards—to attach at the twig ends.

Now I'm scattering leaf cards across the branch surface with randomized lean, bend, and spin so they look naturally varied, plus adding hanging leaf clusters and a streaked gum-bark texture with cream and pinkish tones along the grain.

I'm adding occasional dark scars where randomness dips low, plus a muted color ramp mixing browns and grey-greens, with darker "stocking" bark near the base of the trunk, applying the same bark treatment to the seat branch. Then I'm shifting to the wood plinth, building a pixelated plank texture with seam rows using a tiled box approach.

Now I'm adding a top plate with moss patches, fallen leaves lying flat on the base, and small gumnuts (tiny spheres with lathed caps) scattered on the base and hanging from branches, plus a little brass plaque on the plinth front using a tiny pixel-art texture for faux engraved text. For the koala itself, I'm refining the nose, eyes, cream ear fringes and chest, claws, tufted card details, brow shading, inner thigh coloring, and foot pads, while deciding to skip giving it a leaf to hold. I'm also considering stepped, blocky extrudes to get a pixel-art look for the ears, outlining the circular ear shape with varying column widths per row.

Working out the math for orienting the ear extrusion in 3D -- figuring out the plane normal and perpendicular axes so the ear faces outward correctly, then writing a helper function that computes these direction vectors and extrudes the ear outline centered at the right position on the head.

Working out the offset positioning for the inner ear so it sits forward of the outer ear without clipping through it, placing it at a depth that keeps its front face visible.

For the ear fringe, I'm deciding to build three layered plates instead of individual fur spikes: a larger cream back layer for the fluffy fringe effect, a grey middle layer, and a cream inner front layer, defining the cell grid patterns for each layer.

I'm working through the depth offsets so the outer cream layer peeks out around the edges while grey occupies the visible middle, then positioning the whole ear cluster relative to the head center with appropriate outward-forward orientation.

Now I'm figuring out the stepped-outline helper for the ear geometry, computing the pixel grid origin from width/height and mirroring it for the opposite side while keeping the outline symmetric. Then I'm turning to the fur cards on top of the head and whether the head needs a pixel texture pass.

For the texture pass, I'm sizing the paint cells relative to the head's physical scale so they read as chunky pixels, bumping paint resolution to 2048 for crispness, and starting to define the limited flat color palette with snapped grey ramps for the body paint.

With CREAM and GREY ramps set, I'm writing the fur painting function with light-direction bias, noise variation, and random dithered specks for lighter/darker strand highlights, then moving into defining the chest paint region.

For paws I'm using a dark ramp for pads, with palm spheres scaled at the wrist, and sweeping the arm skin along the chain with varying radii.

Claws are small spike cones placed at each digit tip, oriented along the direction from the mid joint to the tip point so they point outward naturally.

Digit chains use a three-point catmull spline through base, mid, and tip, parented to the wrist joint, with two spans needing two intermediate names.

For hands I'm planning to sweep thin capsule shapes along each digit chain for fingers, then add a short opposable thumb capsule angled off to one side of the wrist for the koala-like hand shape.

Positioning the hand's finger coordinates...

I'm adding toe spacing and a sole sphere under the foot for the thumb-like big toe, then sketching a small pixel-art leaf texture for the eucalyptus branches using a hand-drawn crescent pattern of blue-green shades.

Writing leaf texture generator...

For the stem rows I'll draw a brown center column near the bottom. For leaf card orientation on the twigs, I'm setting the flow vector so eucalyptus leaves hang downward with a slight lean and bend, scattering around 60 cards per branch sweep with a minimum distance spacing, and I'll cap the trunk with a leaf cluster at the top.

I'm also adding hanging bark ribbon strips with a tan/cream pixel texture scattered sparsely around the trunk, plus small gumnut clusters made from tiny spheres with flat cylinder caps mounted on thin stems near the upper branches. For the base, I'm building a wood-textured bottom slab plinth sized to anchor the whole piece.

Now I'm layering a lighter-toned top slab on the plinth, flaring the trunk base radius outward for a natural root effect, and dotting the corners with small green moss-tuft boxes. I'm also placing a small front-facing plaque on the plinth for a label.

Writing pixel text texture...

I'm also adding leaf litter details on the plinth top using angled, flow-rotated leaf cards, and considering whether the koala should hold a leaf in its mouth.

For fur texture, I'm designing a small pixel-art tuft pattern with layered grays, then scattering these tufts across the torso, arms, and head with randomized placement and lean angles, plus a separate cream-toned version for the chest area.

Torso bone hits should carry blended skin weights fine. For the torso sweep, I'll pass radii as an array of values forming a pear shape, wider at the belly since koalas are chunky there, with the top radius overlapping into the neck/head region appropriately.

Shoulders need the arm sweep to start just inside the torso surface so limbs emerge naturally rather than floating outside. For the face, I'm skipping whiskers and brows since koalas don't really have those, and sketching a simple eye texture with a tiny highlight pixel in the top-left corner to give it some shine.

I'm sizing the eye boxes small and flat so the pixel art reads clearly on each face, then moving to the nose: a small pixelated black patch with a subtle highlight dot, placed prominently at the top of the muzzle where a koala's nose flares out.

Now I'm positioning the lower jaw as a small cream-colored box beneath the muzzle, with a joint pivot so it can open, and shaping the head itself as a scaled sphere to get that rounded koala skull form.

I'm also adding small cheek fluff spheres on either side of the face for texture, and then working through the full joint hierarchy -- hips, spine segments, head, jaw, arms with shoulder/elbow/wrist joints plus digit chains, and legs with their own toe joints -- tallying up how many total bones this skeleton needs.

No tail bone is required since koalas don't have one, and the hips serve as the root for the standing pose weighting. I'm double-checking which paint and procedural helper functions (noise, cell paint, catmull splines, pixel art texturing, etc.) I'll actually need to import so I don't end up with unused imports causing errors.

Setting up imports and meta constants...

Defining the body paint for the front chest and lower belly, using the normal direction and position to decide where the cream patch applies.

Now I'm setting up a shared lightness helper for shading variation, plus separate fur paints for the darker hands and feet. For the bark material, I'm layering noise at different scales to build wood grain, adding random scars and dithering, and starting on lower-trunk detailing.

Writing plank texture logic...

Now I'm structuring the koala model's joint hierarchy, starting with hips as the root and building out the spine chain using catmull-rom control points.

Writing head and jaw joints...

Now I'm setting up the limb loop for hips and arms, iterating over left/right sides to generate symmetric chains with hip positions and bend directions for each inner joint.

Adding toe joints and sweep radii...

Setting up the arm chain with shoulder-to-wrist positions, bending the elbow outward and down, then defining finger joint positions along a z-gradient...

I'm noticing the finger base coordinates overlap with the palm sphere position, and checking whether the fingertip embeds correctly into the branch surface for a grip pose -- but I'm spotting a conflict since left and right fingers end up sharing the same z-coordinate, causing overlap.

I need to adjust so hands don't collide at x=0; shortening the finger reach or offsetting hand positions in z should resolve the overlap between left and right grip poses.

Setting the stagger to .08 works, with left and right fingers no longer overlapping in z. I verify the shoulder-to-wrist reach stays under the limit for both arms, then move to building the head parts and ear geometry function.

Still writing ear code...

Still defining ear geometry...

Setting proper paint colors for ears and cream details, then moving to build the trunk using a catmull spline path for branch placement.

Now I'm sweeping the trunk geometry along its path with varying radii and bark coloring, then adjusting the cap styles at the base and top. I'm defining a seat branch using another catmull path with tapering radii, checking that its height roughly aligns with where the koala's bottom would rest against the torso.

Checking for overlap between the trunk's position and the koala's torso, I'm nudging the trunk's z-coordinate slightly back so the koala appears to lean against it with just a bit of natural intersection rather than floating free, then adjusting the seat branch's starting position to match. Now I'm starting to define two upper twig branches extending from the trunk toward the leaves using another catmull curve.

Working through branch placements...

For leaf placement, I'm scattering leaf cards across each twig sweep using randomized distribution, with downward-leaning flow, slight bends, varied sizes, and spin for natural variation.

I'm also planning two leaf textures for color variation, scattering bark strip cards along the trunk, and manually positioning a few small gumnut spheres hanging near specific twig tips with set coordinates.

Each gumnut gets a short stem rod, a tan-brown sphere body, and a flat cylindrical cap on top for detail. For the base, I'm adding a plinth plate with three small flattened, moss-colored mounds placed near the corners to break up the hard edges.

Now I'm scattering flat leaf-litter cards across the top plate with randomized directions, making sure each is attached to the hips bone so they sit correctly. I also want dark corner brackets—small boxes at each corner of the bottom slab—to give it an iron-fitting look.

Checking the model's vertical bounds, the bottom slab sits right at y=0 so nothing clips below ground, and the trunk and leaves stack up fine height-wise. For the torso fur, I'm scattering tufts across the skin surface and splitting them by position and normal direction so the chest gets a cream-colored patch distinct from the gray body fur.

I'm adding smaller tuft scatters to the arms and legs with tighter minimum distance and slightly smaller card sizes, then doing the head similarly while filtering out the front face area so tufts don't clutter the eyes, and making sure they don't poke through the separately modeled ears.

Now I'm turning to cheek fluff, deciding to just scatter extra tufts directly onto the cream cheek spheres rather than treating fluff separately, applying that to both sides. I'm also tallying up the rough part count across hands and feet digits with their sweeps and claws, estimating around forty-plus parts total just for the extremities.

Overall I figure total parts will land around a hundred or so including texture cards, well within budget, with flat colors for cream and other base hues. For the leaf textures, I'm writing a pixel-texture generator that builds a tapered leaf shape with dark/mid/light shading and a vein color, computing width per row based on a sine-curve taper from tip to base.

Writing leaf texture function...

Writing bark texture pattern...

Checking types for the limb chain output, hit filters, scatter options, and card rendering calls, plus confirming the Cell type import and color definitions are all consistent.

Now I'm defining helper functions for fur lighting and painting - computing brightness values from normals and noise, then using those to pick colors from a ramp with dithering, followed by a body paint function using edge detection via noise.

I'm still working out the head and muzzle shading, distinguishing cream chin/throat regions from grey using y-position thresholds softened by noise, and setting up a lighter grey ramp specifically for the muzzle area.

Now I'm placing the eyes slightly above head center with wide spacing to match a koala's look, and sketching a small mouth line beneath the muzzle front.

I decide to skip the mouth line and philtrum for simplicity, keeping just the nose with subtle nostril texture dots. I'm also double-checking that variables like jaw, frame, stepped, tileBox, pixelArt, rng, catmull, and limb are all actually used before assembling the hands, foot soles, and rump fluff sphere.

Now I'm working out the plinth's tile box signature with a single random seed, then moving to painting the torso body with sphere-based hips. For the leaves, I'm scattering surface cards across branches b1, b2, b4, and the trunk top with different counts (70, 70, 30, 40) and a minimum distance threshold, leaving the leaf cards untinted.

I'm defining a flow function that gives each leaf card a slight directional sway using sine and cosine offsets, confirming it matches the expected direction input type. Finally I return the root node and prepare to write the file, importing the Paint type with noise support.
